Hi Alex / Priya, thanks for the details. A few technical clarifications and options from the Redwood side: 

1) PrivateLink (recommended path)
   - We expose an NLB (Network Load Balancer) in our serving VPC and you create an Interface VPC Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) in your VPC that connects to the NLB.
   - Benefits: traffic stays on the AWS network, no public IPs need to be allowlisted on your side, minimal routing changes.
   - Egress behavior: if you consume through the interface endpoint, outbound responses traverse AWS internal network and generally do not require you to allow specific public egress IPs. If you have outbound rules that restrict egress to a set of external IPs, we can provide a small set of EIPs (see note below) used for callbacks/outbound webhooks.

2) VPC Peering (alternative)
   - We support VPC peering but it requires non-overlapping CIDRs and proper route table entries on both sides. Peering can be simpler for some internal-only flows but increases blast radius compared to PrivateLink.

3) Egress IPs / EIP ranges
   - For procurement: we can provision a small set of elastic IPs for egress and provide them as a CIDR or explicit IP list. Example placeholder EIPs for planning: 54.23.12.45, 54.23.12.46, 54.23.12.47. We will provide the final list after network scoping and allocation (typically 48-72 hours lead time once the network model is agreed).

4) TLS / mutual auth
   - We support TLS 1.2+ and can enable mTLS if you require client certificates. For most customers, standard TLS with validated certs is sufficient; mTLS adds an extra configuration step on both sides.

5) Firewall rules (recommended minimal set)
   - If using PrivateLink: Allow inbound from your VPC to the Interface endpoint (no public inbound required). On your firewall, allow outbound to the AWS Interface Endpoint IPs on 443.
   - If using NLB/peering: Allow inbound 443 from our serving NLB EIPs (we will provide final list) and ensure route to the peered VPC.

Attachments: networking-checklist.xlsx (please populate)

Next steps:
- If you confirm PrivateLink, we'll schedule the 30-min network call and begin allocating EIPs (if required).
- I'll produce a short network diagram and final EIP list within 48-72 hours after the checklist is returned.

Happy to hop on the call; I can do Mon 4/19 10:30-11:30 PT or Tue 4/20 9-10 PT.
